rv.q: Gray does a fine job of communicating the play’s cruel, acrid humour, much of which relies on the shock of blunt honesty and deadpan deliveries of callous statements.
It’s a clever if chilly comedy.
Broken Nose Theatre are currently presenting a splendid revival of The Ugly One at Arcola Theatre , and it is well worth catching.
Almost twenty years after it was written, von Mayenburg’s satire has lost none of its bite.
His refreshing revival of The Ugly One allows a reconsideration of a powerful parable worthy of Franz Kafka by one of the most vital of contemporary German playwrights.
If you’re confident in your attention span when it comes to pacy dialogue, even when deliberately deprived of catchier sounds and light effects, you will have a glorious, bizarre, fun time.
At just an hour long, it is perfect as part of an evening out with friends.
Broken Nose Theatre’s take on The Ugly One left us feeling amused, bemused, and thoughtful.

Segal strike the balance perfectly between innocence and malevolence, as Lette’s newfound power sees him inflict the same injustice he once suffered on his colleague, stealing his ideas and passing them off as his own.

cn.t: Critics find this absurdist satire on beauty and identity mostly sharp and timely, praising the nimble ensemble. A few find the direction too clinical and the staging too bare, leaving the comedy feeling shallow.
